clue.text: Disney actors who overact? Draw in Gtr London town

blocks.note: Walt Disney, the film producer
a ham is an actor who overplays a part
to draw a vehicle along is to tow it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about scenery-chewing Disney performers, followed by an instruction to sketch something in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: WALTHAMSTOW is a district of north-east London; Gtr is short for Greater, as in Greater London.
explanation.definitionFit: Walthamstow is a place within the Greater London boundary, so it is an example of such a town.

clue.text: Dancing, the Empress Maud in a song

blocks.note: waltzing is one kind of dancing
the Empress Matilda, also called Maud, claimed the English throne in the twelfth century

explanation.surface: A medieval empress is pictured dancing within the lines of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Empress Matilda was known as Maud in English, so the two names are one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltzing Matilda is the famous Australian folk ballad about a swagman, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Branch on top of English box

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on top of another comes first, above it in the column

blocks.note: a cut branch of a tree is a log
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tree branch has fallen on top of an English crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A loge is a private box or compartment in a theatre, so the word is a synonym for that sense of box.

clue.text: Greek girl drinking litre, last from fridge ...

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something inside, so one piece swallows another
the last from a word means only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a girl's name
L is the symbol for litre
the final letter of fridge

explanation.surface: A Greek girl gulps a litre of something cold from the fridge, with the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The litre goes inside the girl's name after its third letter, and the fridge's last letter is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek person, the name the ancient Greeks used for themselves.

clue.text: ... a wine shown in doctor's magazine

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, here with the possessive
Elle is a fashion magazine

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a wine is advertised in a doctor's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a standard crossword doctor; the apostrophe supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the Moselle river in Germany, so it is an example of a wine.

clue.text: Cast went on list in Hollywood

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so the letters are thrown into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film's cast was put on a list in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the film's actors, apt for Hollywood, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, mocking its glitter and superficial glamour.

clue.text: A follower of the news?

blocks.note: surface reading: a person who keeps up with current affairs
setter's reading: the broadcast item that comes straight after the news bulletin on TV and radio

explanation.walkthrough: A follower sounds like a person, but here it is the programme item that follows the news in the schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: On British television and radio the predictions of rain and sunshine traditionally come right after the news bulletin.

clue.text: Take a meal outside, that's something easy to do

blocks.note: first meaning: to eat outdoors, as a verb
second meaning: an easy task

explanation.surface: Eating outdoors is presented as an effortless task.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for eating an outdoor meal and an informal noun for a task requiring little effort.

clue.text: Examine burn on child

blocks.note: to sear is to scorch or burn
CH is a common abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A doctor is asked to look at a burn on a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To search something is to look through or inspect it carefully, a synonym for examine.

clue.text: Criminal, evil European girl

blocks.note: ill can mean evil, as in ill will
E is the abbreviation for European
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A wicked European woman is described as a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illegal is against the law, so the adjective is a synonym for criminal.

clue.text: Worker settling in fine US city

indicators.note: something settling in somewhere takes up residence inside it

blocks.note: safe can mean fine, unharmed
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer moves to a pleasant American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital of the US state of New Mexico, so it is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Cape carried by Jonathan (Azed)

indicators.note: the answer is carried within the following words, sitting across the boundary between them

blocks.note: the end of the first name runs into the start of the pen-name

explanation.surface: A headland belongs to Jonathan Crowther, who sets crosswords as Azed.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the pseudonym of Jonathan Crowther, a rival setter at the Observer. The Naze is a headland on the Essex coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A naze is a headland or promontory, the same thing as a cape jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Ring her about feeble leader

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: to ring someone is to give them a bell, a phone call
taken as written
wet is British slang for feeble or weedy

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone a woman about a weak leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring her reads as BELL HER, and the pair goes about WET; a wet is a feeble person in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the lead sheep of a flock wearing a bell, hence anyone who takes the lead or sets a trend.

clue.text: Tired and silly drunk in here?

definitions.text: Tired and silly drunk in here?

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person might end up weary and giddy after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a place where you could get tired and silly drunk, with the question mark flagging the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery makes whisky and other spirits, so it is a place where visitors might well become intoxicated.

clue.text: Arthropod's reported smell, one by deep ground

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read
something ground is crushed up, so its letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: a scent is a smell, which is said like a coin's name
the Roman numeral for one
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A many-legged creature's scent is noted, alongside something being ground up deep.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged invertebrate, and centipedes belong to the arthropod group with insects and spiders.

clue.text: A large candle, to the right in front of church

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A big candle stands on the right, in front of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch was originally a large candle or flaming brand carried for light, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Entice one from agency, latest of eight

indicators.note: the latest of something is the one that comes last, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an employment agency
the final letter of eight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lure a worker away from a staffing agency, the newest of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to lure or attract them into doing something, a synonym for entice.

clue.text: Long crumpled T-shirt

indicators.note: a crumpled garment has been crushed out of shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A description of an oversized, wrinkled T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the shirt; it is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To thirst for something is to crave it, so the verb is a synonym for long, as in longing for.

clue.text: Disposed towards good direction in a film

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are laid out differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A character in a film is inclined to take a decent course.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw Dogs is a 1971 thriller directed by Sam Peckinpah, starring Dustin Hoffman, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Extend prison term

blocks.note: first meaning: to lengthen or pull out
second meaning: slang for a period served in jail

explanation.surface: A judge lengthens a convict's sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to lengthen and a slang noun for time served behind bars.

clue.text: Find ladder below

blocks.note: a ladder in tights is a run in American English
down means below, lower down

explanation.surface: Someone locates a ladder lying underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a ladder is a vertical tear in tights or stockings, called a run elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down something is to track it down after searching, so the phrasal verb is a synonym for find.

clue.text: Everyman's dog?

blocks.note: first meaning: Everyman is the compiler of this very puzzle
second meaning: a breed of gun dog, such as the Irish or English variety

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests a pet belonging to Everyman; read 's as 'is', and the setter calls himself one.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a crossword is called its setter, and a setter is also a long-haired gun dog breed.

clue.text: Impatient on train, let loose

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed from their order and can fall anyhow

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A passenger grows restless on a train and is finally released.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intolerant cannot put up with things, close in sense to impatient and unwilling to endure delay.

clue.text: International trial

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... match, an international game of cricket or rugby
second meaning: a trial or examination

explanation.walkthrough: International looks like an adjective; it is a noun, an international match, which in cricket is called a Test.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is a match between national cricket or rugby sides, and the word also means an experiment or exam.

clue.text: Layabout could make one cry nicking pound

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, and the thief holds the loot inside

blocks.note: to sob is to cry
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An idler might reduce someone to tears by stealing their money.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person, a synonym for layabout.

clue.text: Afloat in river crossing heart of Devon

indicators.note: the water crossing something here lies around it, taking the piece within
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the Solent, the stretch of water between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire, once a river valley
the central letter of Devon

explanation.surface: A boat stays afloat on a river flowing through the middle of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afloat' reads as being on water, apt for a river; it means financially sound. The Solent is a strait off the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that is afloat is keeping its head above water financially, which means able to pay its debts.

clue.text: Officially excused from duty, one touring vale abroad

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters wander

blocks.note: taken as written
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier freed from duty goes travelling through a foreign valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on leave has authorised time away from work or military service.

clue.text: Naughty night by aunt? Not in the least

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters do not stay in line

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if their aunt had a wild night out, and the answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is anything but true means it is not at all true, an idiom of emphatic denial.
